title: Digital kidney-biopsy damage features are associated with later graft loss
summary: Deep-learning image analysis quantified tissue damage in 789 kidney-transplant biopsy slides from two cohorts. A damage score from 12-month biopsies was associated with subsequent graft loss in both cohorts. Baseline-score survival association was not confirmed in the smaller Australian cohort, and clinical utility remains untested.
ai_technology: Mask R-CNN and U-Net histopathology analysis
organization: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; University of Sydney

source_review.scope: Primary full-text bibliographic dates, computational classification Methods, held-out Results and explicit cohort/reference limitations.

evidence.tested: Networks were developed on 60 selected biopsy slides and tested on 33 others. The pipeline then analyzed 478 baseline and 311 twelve-month slides from 404 GoCAR and 212 AUSCAD participants. In 200 GoCAR and 111 AUSCAD twelve-month biopsies, composite tissue/inflammation scores were associated with later death-censored graft loss; thresholds were derived in GoCAR.
evidence.unknown: This is retrospective image/outcome analysis of previously collected cohorts, not prospective evaluation of a frozen clinical tool. GoCAR supplies both selected model-development slides and outcome analyses, with exact patient overlap not separated here. Baseline ITAS survival association was not confirmed in AUSCAD. Observational associations, selected thresholds, limited graft-loss events and cohort differences prevent causal, treatment-benefit or universal surrogate-endpoint claims.
evidence.ai_role: Neural tissue/immune-cell segmentation supplied quantitative damage features, which ordinary survival analysis related to subsequent graft outcomes.
